key_insight: An explainable machine-learning pipeline using acoustic speech features can classify Parkinson’s disease with high accuracy while highlighting the specific voice biomarkers driving each prediction.
clinical_relevance: If validated externally, this approach could support scalable, non-invasive screening or triage using ordinary speech recordings.
method: 756 voice recordings from 252 subjects (188 PD, 64 controls) were preprocessed and z-score normalized.
Five classifiers were compared under subject-independent GroupKFold cross-validation: KNN, XGBoost, Random Forest, SVM, and Naive Bayes.
SHAP was used to interpret feature contributions and identify the most informative acoustic biomarkers.
evidence_signal: KNN performed best, achieving 92.10% accuracy, 94.50% F1, and 98.09% precision on the study’s cross-validated evaluation.
watch_item: Performance was reported on a public dataset, so external validation across different recording conditions, languages, and populations is still needed before real-world use.
paper_title: An Explainable AI-Driven Classification Framework for Parkinson's Disease Detection via Acoustic Speech Features: A Comparative Machine Learning Study
